# Gelabber v0.9.2

Integrated through #484 to #495 into `v0.9` and the version PR into `main`.

A design pass over both clients after a UI critique of the web and the
native app: Live gets its own colour, rows get real menus, settings share
one layout, contrast and screen-reader names improve, and the wording is
German and plain. The native app can now copy, paste and select message
text. Arch installs in one command, and the web client points browser users
to the desktop app. There is no database migration, and `.env`,
`compose.yaml` and `Caddyfile` change only in their image pins.

## Both clients

- **Live has its own colour (#492).** LIVE badges, the call bar's Live
  button, the live hint and the live toast use an on-air coral instead of
  danger red, so Live no longer reads as a warning. Verlassen, Sperren and
  errors stay red; unread counts are amber like the other unread marks. The
  colour comes from the theme with the same contrast floor as the others,
  and turns away from an accent close to it (Ristretto). The live hint and
  toast say "Zuschauen" and join and start watching in one step; from
  another call they say "Zum Kanal". Your own Live shows a small "Mit Ton" /
  "Ohne Ton" tag instead of a bar over the name.
- **Row menus (#493).** Channels, servers, DMs and the home tile have a menu
  on right click, long press, Shift+F10, the context-menu key or a "…"
  button: mark read, mute for a length, notification level and the
  notification settings, plus edit and delete for managers and channel
  actions for categories. Hidden row actions leave the Tab order and the
  accessibility tree. Choosing "Wie der Server" during a timed mute keeps the
  mute's end.
- **Call shortcuts (#489).** The shortcut sheet has a group "Im
  Sprachkanal" (Strg+Umschalt+M, Strg+Umschalt+D, push-to-talk, K for Kino).
  Every call bar control has a tooltip with its shortcut, and the mic and
  headset say "Stumm" and "Taub" when they are off. Natively, Esc closes an
  open popover or menu first instead of marking the conversation read.
- **Plain text and German terms (#488).** Reply lines, previews, toasts and
  system notifications show plain text instead of markdown marks, with
  spoilers hidden. DM toasts name the person once. Search hits use the
  message list's date format and mark the matched words. "Voice", "Account",
  "Mic-Gain" and "Stream-Ton" are now "Sprache", "Konto",
  "Mikrofonverstärkung" and "Live-Ton"; the call dialog is "Audio & Video".
  A failed reaction on a removed message says so.
- **Settings (#486).** Server settings mark the section in view in their
  anchor row. Allgemein says what saves at once and what needs Speichern,
  and a disabled Speichern says "Keine Änderungen.". Settings rows share
  one width. "Mikrofon testen" sits under the microphone select, so it is
  visible when the dialog opens. Loose voice rooms join an existing
  "Sprachkanäle" category instead of a second heading.
- **Contrast and screen readers (#485).** Hints, timestamps, placeholders
  and disabled labels reach 4.5:1 on every surface, in built-in and custom
  themes. The selected server no longer has an amber ring, so amber means
  keyboard focus only. Speaking members get small level bars and "spricht"
  in their name; unread counts say "ungelesen".
- **Voice rooms (#487).** Tiles show speaking once (avatar ring and
  "Spricht" line, no green border). Overview cards show the status line and
  a free seat. A room you are alone in asks "Fehlt noch jemand?" with an
  "Einladen" button. The mic test meters match the quick settings' meter.

## Desktop

- **Copy and paste through the system clipboard (#484).** Ctrl+V pastes
  text and pictures from other apps, and "Text kopieren" and "Link
  kopieren" reach the system clipboard. They stayed inside the app before.
- **Select message text (#491).** Message bodies, quotes, code, link
  previews and search hits can be selected by dragging, also across
  messages, and copied with Ctrl+C. Names, times and buttons stay
  unselectable, and hidden spoilers stay out of copies. The selection colour
  is Chromium's blue, in text fields too.
- **Setup screen and update notice (#490).** "Server verbinden" uses the
  sign-in frame and the active theme. Connection errors are plain German
  (refused, timeout, unknown host, TLS, not a Gelabber server …) with the
  system text as details, and the address is checked against the server's
  API. Settings › App collects updates and close-to-tray. The update notice
  uses the theme, sits below the header and shows a progress bar while it
  downloads.
- The speaking ring has one edge, and scrollbars float over the content and
  fade after scrolling (#487).

## Web

- **Desktop app offer (#495).** Settings › App starts with a "Desktop-App"
  card for Windows (installer and SmartScreen steps) or Linux (the Arch
  one-liner, or the tarball). After signing in, a desktop browser on Windows
  or x64 Linux gets one toast, once per browser, pointing there.
- At phone width the unread badge sits on the server tile's corner instead
  of covering the initials (#487).

## Linux (Arch)

- **One-command install (#494).**
  `curl -fsSL https://till-und-scholler-ai-slop.github.io/Gelabber/install.sh | sudo sh`
  checks the pinned key fingerprint, adds `[gelabber]` to `pacman.conf`
  once and installs `gelabber-desktop`. It goes live with this release's
  Pages deployment.

## Upgrade notes

- The image pins `GELABBER_{API,WEB,MEDIA}_IMAGE` move together to
  `v0.9.2`. The server code is unchanged; the web image carries the new web
  client.
- **Rollback, server:** go back to the v0.9.1 image set, all three
  together. The database is unchanged.
- **Desktop, Windows:** the native app offers the update itself.
- **Desktop, Linux (Arch):** `pacman -Syu`.
- **GitHub Pages:** approve the `github-pages` deployment after the
  release, so `install.sh` and the desktop app offer's Linux line work.

## Open

- Paste and copy in the running native app (#484, #491) are covered by
  unit tests only; the build machine has no display.
- Strg+Umschalt+M / D in Firefox were not pressed in a real call (#489).
- The native `mediasoup_loopback` test failed twice on busy CI runners
  with "no decoded frames for video/AV1" and passed on rerun; the PRs did
  not touch media code.
- The parity shots still show two "Sprachkanäle" headings until the shared
  parity database is re-seeded (#486).
